hints: Focus on what the Boltzmann curve really shows, the spread of molecular energies at one temperature.
Remember that raising temperature increases average energy, so fewer molecules stay at low energy and more spread to high energy.
Think about how the peak must flatten and shift to keep total area constant, and check whether X or Y mark an energy value on the x-axis.
walkthrough:
**Read what the axes mean**

Think of this curve as a snapshot of how energy is shared out. The x-axis is molecular energy $E$, the y-axis is proportion of molecules with that energy.

No molecules have zero energy, most have a moderate energy at the peak, and a few have very high energy in the long tail.

**Predict the effect of higher temperature**

Higher temperature means higher average kinetic energy. So the whole distribution spreads out toward higher energy.

Because the total number of molecules is fixed, the area under the curve must stay the same. The peak gets lower and broader, and the most probable energy moves to higher $E$.

**Check what X and Y actually are**

X and Y are vertical arrows. They show a proportion of molecules (y-value), not an energy (x-value).

Activation energy $E_a$ and enthalpy change $\Delta H$ are horizontal distances along the energy axis, so a vertical line cannot represent them.

**Pick the correct description**

Raising $T$ shifts the maximum to the right (higher energy) and lowers its height. Only the shift to the right is listed correctly.

options.A: Incorrect. Raising temperature spreads molecules over a wider energy range, so the peak flattens. The height of the maximum decreases, not increases, to keep total area constant.
options.B: Correct. Higher temperature gives a higher average and most probable energy. The peak broadens, lowers, and moves to the right toward higher molecular energy E.
options.C: Incorrect. Activation energy is marked as a position on the energy axis, usually a vertical line at $E = E_a$. X is just a tiny vertical height showing the small proportion of molecules with very high energy.
options.D: Incorrect. Enthalpy change $\Delta H$ is an energy difference on the x-axis, not a population. Y is the vertical height of the peak, showing the proportion of molecules with the most probable energy.
